about: The evidence page, as one Task Object. scripts/build_site.py renders it into site/evidence/index.html. The words are kept as written; the build fills each served folder's files from site/evidence/ and the last live check from its saved record, and stops when a served folder or a folder of the repository's evidence/ has no line here.
title: Evidence | ta-amps
description: Every dated evidence folder this site serves, what each one shows and its files, the evidence kept in the repository on GitHub, and a dated check of what answered.
heading: Evidence and status
lead: Dated results and what is live. Every folder in the first list is served with this site, so each of its files opens here.

live.heading: What answered at the last check
live.lead: One moment, kept as it was: a plain curl of each public health address, with no credentials. It is a dated snapshot, not a monitor.

notes.https://eranos.ta-amps.workers.dev/v1/he: Eranos keeps its health check at /api/health, on the next line.

snapshot.how: plain curl -sS -m 20 of each public URL, GET, no credentials, one try each

served.heading: Served with this site
served.lead: Newest first. Each line says what the folder shows, and its files follow.

folders.title: A real run, replayed
folders.line: One request built and reviewed from start to finish on a local copy of Tessera: the trace, Tessera’s records read back, the record of each replayed step, and the four files the builder stored.

link.label: See it replayed on How it works

folders.title: The last live check
folders.line: One plain curl of each public health address, saved as it came back, with the time it ran. The part above reads it.

folders.title: The public record of the real runs
folders.line: Each recorded attempt at a real run on a local copy of Tessera with Meta’s {{model:muse-spark-1.3}} at contributor tier, with its outcome and recorded spend, the two runs that finished, and the hosted health probes taken that morning.

link.label: See it replayed on How it works

folders.title: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}, as memory
folders.line: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} tuned to recall Task Objects from its own weights, on Kaggle’s free GPUs and example data: the results, a chart and the verification record.

folders.title: How the v6 film was made
folders.line: Production records for the v6 film’s cuts and their automated video checks. The checks record failures, such as frozen frames, and the files keep them.

folders.title: How the v3 film was made
folders.line: Production records for the v3 film’s cuts, their automated video checks, which record failures, and a pixel and motion audit.

served.not_served: Its raw files stay in the source, not on this site.

source.heading: In the repository on GitHub
source.lead: This evidence sits in the repository’s evidence folder, which the site does not serve. It is in Agora’s repository on GitHub, under these paths; the newest folders arrive there when this version is merged.
source.same: The same files as the served folder

items.line: The last live check's saved Eranos answer, kept here because its raw text holds a word this site does not show; the live check above shows what it said.
{{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} tuned for tool calls: the run record, which lists every file it used.
Descriptive counts of the hackathon’s public repositories as Tasks and Task Objects. Nothing in it ranks or judges a team.
The integration snapshot: merged pull requests and repository and portal checks, with their limits.
The readiness snapshot: repository checks, onboarding and protocol stress, with their limits.
The training and community snapshot that status.json points to.
How the v2 film was made: its production records and a script that rechecks them.
Training records for separate small adapters, one per job. Its batched evaluation ran out of GPU memory, so it claims no score.
Local evaluations of adapter memory and the model shim's router, image and speech checks, a many-worker scaling run and a fault-injection test.
Offline benchmarks over the seed-pack library: self-learning retrieval with compiled shims, a scenario matrix built on Meta’s ARE and a partner compute cascade, all run locally with no remote spend.
